newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen steady to up at open, awaits data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen steady to up at open, awaits data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open steady to slightly higher on Monday, with personal income and consumption data giving the markets some initial direction on the final day of the fiscal quarter.
The Chicago Purchasing Manager's Index for June, due at 1400 GMT, would also draw attention, analysts said.
After that the recently-volatile stock market could shift its focus to a meeting of key Federal Reserve policy makers, which starts on Tuesday.
"Barring a surprise in the personal income and consumption data, we could hold steady until tomorrow," Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 1.35 points at 898.25.
On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished a week of wild swings by closing up around 33 points at 7,688.
